headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow can egress broadly while Pathway is local-only, creating default data-flow and compliance exposure; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are otherwise limited by missing shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has no browser or clipboard surface, and Pathway exposes no filesystem, MCP, or stdin/stdout bridge. With no documented shared channel, there is no plausible default prompt-injection path between them.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Airflow output into Pathway prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe Airflow logs into Pathway prompts.
Disable any future shared clipboard or queue bridge.
Add provenance tags before any manual copy-paste.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, so if it processes sensitive files, it can transmit them outward. Pathway is local-only with no network egress, so the main leakage risk is one-way from Airflow rather than mutual exfiltration. The pair still creates default exposure if shared data reaches Airflow.
conditions: IF sensitive files are fed into Airflow tasks, outbound leakage is possible.
IF Pathway is later granted network egress, the leakage surface expands.
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of Airflow tasks.
Route secrets through redacted placeholders only.
Review Airflow task logs for payload echoes.
Maintain Pathway as network-isolated.
Add a preflight check that blocks sensitive datasets.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow can orchestrate networked automation, but Pathway cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable write surface, direct capability conflict is limited and requires extra orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents shared mutable OAuth scopes, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Keep Pathway read-only.
Use a lock file if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate downstream pipeline outputs, and Pathway can consume data-processing outputs, so A-to-B handoff is plausible. Because Pathway has no explicit verification or critical-evaluation surface in the profile, erroneous Airflow outputs could cascade into later processing without a built-in check.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are fed directly into Pathway jobs, errors can propagate.
IF Pathway is configured to trust upstream artifacts without validation, cascading failure increases.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require schema checks on Airflow outputs.
Compare sample records before ingestion.
Reject malformed or missing fields.
Log provenance for each handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while Pathway is local-only; if regulated data flows through Airflow, residency or retention controls can diverge from Pathway's local processing. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so this is a general compliance exposure rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF EU PII or other regulated data is processed by Airflow, residency review is required.
IF retention policies differ between the two pipelines, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before routing.
Keep regulated data out of Airflow egress paths.
Document retention for both systems.
Add a residency check to pipeline review.
Use separate environments for regulated workloads.
